analysis:
All changes in this batch are test-only files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Autopilot/. No production code, wire handling, crypto, attestation, or authorization logic is modified, so no runtime attack surface or regression is introduced by these diffs.

Behaviors the new tests assert, which should be checked in the production source (not supplied here):
- AutopilotPlacementHoldTests.swift: a coordinator-commanded placement hold keeps a model resident. Held slots are excluded from evictableModelSlots (lines 9-24), from cold-load slot-cap eviction (57-84) and from memory eviction (86-99). Held weights get no reclaim credit in capacity reporting (101-119). Idle unload waits for hold expiry plus the idle timeout (26-55). A hold ends when the weight hash becomes unverifiable (139-167) or on admin unload (169-180).
- ModelAutopilotTests.swift:121-165: hold_seconds is validated to 0...86400 and only allowed with a load target. The busy detail field is optional on the wire.
- AutopilotSnapshotCodingTests.swift:110-138: snake_case wire coding for the new report fields, plus a DaemonStateFile round-trip.

Relevant to TB-002 and TB-007 availability. A hold lets the coordinator (trusted) pin GPU memory for at most 24h. It is bounded, and the tests show it does not block admin unload or hash-unverifiable release. This is a DoS-resource-control design to confirm in production: the validation bound, that the hold is not honored when the autopilot session or revision is inactive, and that heldModels reporting leaks no sensitive data (model ids and expiry only, already public via heartbeats). The tests imply those controls exist, but the implementation is outside the supplied evidence. No finding is raised. T-041 and the cache/KEK posture are untouched.
